bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to employment; prohibiting job misclassification; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 181.03, subdivision 1.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 181.03, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Prohibited practices.
An employer may not, directly or indirectly and with intent to defraud:
(1) cause any employee to give a receipt for wages for a greater amount than that actually paid to the employee for services rendered;
(2) directly or indirectly demand or receive from any employee any rebate or refund from the wages owed the employee under contract of employment with the employer; [-or -]
(3) in any manner make or attempt to make it appear that the wages paid to any employee were greater than the amount actually paid to the employee[-.-][+; or +]

[+(4) if an employer has a formal job classification and compensation plan, place an employee in a job classification or job category or provide a job title that misrepresents the employee's experience or actual job duties and responsibilities. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to employment; prohibiting job misclassification; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 181.03, subdivision 1.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 181.03, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Prohibited practices.
An employer may not, directly or indirectly and with intent to defraud:
(1) cause any employee to give a receipt for wages for a greater amount than that actually paid to the employee for services rendered;
(2) directly or indirectly demand or receive from any employee any rebate or refund from the wages owed the employee under contract of employment with the employer;
(3) in any manner make or attempt to make it appear that the wages paid to any employee were greater than the amount actually paid to the employee; or

(4) if an employer has a formal job classification and compensation plan, place an employee in a job classification or job category or provide a job title that misrepresents the employee's experience or actual job duties and responsibilities.
additions: (4) if an employer has a formal job classification and compensation plan, place an employee in a job classification or job category or provide a job title that misrepresents the employee's experience or actual job duties and responsibilities.
